article.name: Cognee-RS
article.summary: Cognee-RS is a Rust port of Cognee that ingests text, files, URLs and code into persistent knowledge graphs with vector indexes, then exposes remember, recall, improve and forget operations. It uses relational, graph and vector stores and supports multiple provider and SDK surfaces. This assessment reflects selected source and documentation at the verified main head; no runtime or benchmark was run.

who_what.text: The curated catalog lists ordinal 135 as Cognee-RS, slug cognee-rs, with the explicit locator https://github.com/topoteretes/cognee-rs. The pinned Atlas entry is retained only for roster identity and locator attribution, not as assessment evidence.

The official public repository page identifies main as its default branch. The official main commit feed reports full head a70bcab30059b674b98822a7bdff1570a69dfeb7, updated 2026-11-25T08:02:24Z; the reviewed documentation and source links pin that commit.
The project describes itself as a Rust port of the Python Cognee library. It is a library and CLI with language bindings; the HTTP server is referenced by the docs but is not part of this repository.

architecture.text: The system composes add/ingest, cognify and search. Cognify classifies and chunks input, extracts graph entities and relationships with an LLM, summarizes and persists graph/vector artifacts; the high-level memory API wraps this as remember, recall, improve and forget.

Memory spans three backends: relational storage tracks documents, datasets, sessions and provenance; the graph stores entities and relationships; and the vector store indexes chunks, entities, summaries and edge facts. Defaults are SQLite, embedded Ladybug graph storage, and embedded LanceDB; alternate backends and providers are feature/configuration dependent.

DataPoint is the common record model with a UUID, timestamps, version/type fields, metadata, dataset membership and pipeline provenance such as source pipeline, task, node set and content hash. The cognify persistence layer writes ownership rows before graph, vectors and edge evidence, deduplicating shared artifacts across document groups.

Recall orchestrates multiple retrieval strategies. The default hybrid route combines vector matches over chunks, summaries, entities and edge facts with one-hop graph expansion and an LLM completion; routing can choose lexical, temporal, coding-rules, graph and other strategies.

behavior.text: Write: remember adds input, runs cognify and by default an improve pass. Ingestion hashes/deduplicates and stores source material; cognify extracts and summarizes per document and persists resulting graph/vector items plus per-item ownership/provenance records. Code-repository memory has a separate deterministic graph path that does not require an LLM.

Update/correction: the documented update replaces one document while retaining its data ID, removes its prior derived memory, re-adds it and cognifies again. Improve can enrich or personalize graph/session context from feedback. These APIs do not by themselves establish correction accuracy or guarantee all stale derived content is absent.

Delete: forget/delete supports all owned data, a dataset, or a data item and cascades through relational, graph, vector and file stores; dry-run previews are documented. Run-scoped sweeps remove artifacts produced by failed cognify runs, while shared artifacts remain when another owner still claims them.

Retrieval: recall auto-routes by query unless a search type is supplied, applies graph/session scopes and dataset filters, and can return context without an answer when completion is unavailable. Retrieval modes have different capabilities and constraints; for example, batch triplet search loads the whole graph and is documented as more expensive on large stores.

Scope: datasets are the principal organizational and ownership boundary, optionally tenant-scoped. Search supports dataset filters, while sessions are keyed by owner and may be shared through readable-dataset hooks in configured bindings. Node-set selection exists but is documented as type/name subgraph filtering rather than a complete general-purpose node-set query surface; authorization behavior depends on the caller/hosting layer.

Provenance/evidence: DataPoints include pipeline/task/node-set/source-content provenance. The relational ledger records per-dataset and per-data-item ownership of nodes and edges to support deletion and rollback; edge evidence is also persisted. This tracks lineage/ownership, not a guarantee that generated answers expose claim-level citations or that cited evidence supports every statement.

Efficiency and observability: the pipeline uses streaming/bounded document work, single-writer ordering, incremental cognify markers and embedded local-default stores. OpenTelemetry spans can cover pipeline stages when telemetry is enabled and activated; structured logging is documented. README speed figures are upstream claims, not independently measured here.

Known constraints include an in-process-only serialized writer model for file-backed graph storage (cross-process locking is out of scope), provider/model dependency for LLM-based extraction and completion, partial node-set semantics, and a recall mode whose batch triplet search can scan the full graph.

metrics.evidence: The source documents retrieval routes and context-only fallback, but no gold answerable/unanswerable cases were executed or adjudicated.
Update replaces and re-cognifies an item, but no correction probes or stale-value rate were measured.
Source describes cascading deletion and run sweeps; no post-delete probes examined residual content in stores, backups, logs, or copies.
Dataset/session scoping is visible in source and docs; no cross-user, cross-dataset, or tenant isolation workload was run.
Pipeline provenance and edge evidence exist, but no generated answer was adjudicated for claim-level support or citation coverage.
The README gives speed figures as product claims; no timing distribution was collected in this review.
No timed ingestion-to-correct-recall workload was run.
No token or provider-cost accounting was performed.
No corpus storage-size or per-item measurement was collected.

limits.text: This is a source-only review of selected current README, architecture/concepts/operations documentation, data model, persistence, scope, deletion and provenance code. It does not establish behavior across every backend, binding, feature combination, provider, or error path.

No Cognee-RS runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run. Retrieval quality, abstention, correction, complete erasure, isolation, latency, write-to-recall delay, token/cost use and storage efficiency remain unmeasured.

The documentation says cross-process coordination for file-backed graph storage is outside the current Rust design, and describes node sets as a partial tagging/scoping primitive. Deployments needing multi-process writes or strong tenant boundaries require host-level design and verification.
Whether a recalled answer is factually supported depends on the selected retriever, model and consumer behavior; stored lineage and edge evidence alone do not prove user-facing citation quality.

benchmark.note: No Cognee-RS runtime, tests or benchmark execution was performed. Source observations and README performance claims are not project benchmark results.
